Provision for bypassing in-built Protection release 21. All ACB shall have Under Voltage release tripping provision 3.0 GENERAL TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS A. Retrofit breaker compartment 1. A single common solution with same hardware is required as a common solution for all the breakers liste d. All the breakers should have closed door operation. 2. Existing bus bars shall be retained as it is with minor modification if required. 3. The circuit breakers shall be mounted on a withdrawable assembly which shall move horizontally from s ervice position to isolate position and back. For complete withdrawal from the panel, the assembly shall bri ng the breaker completely out of the panel for further removal using telescopic trolleys. 4. The existing door of the breaker to be replaced with new door with proper sealing to avoid any opening or dust ingress in the compartment. 5. Testing of the breaker shall be possible in TEST position from local control as well as remote. 6. Necessary guide channels shall be provided in the breaker compartments for proper alignment of auxilia ry contacts when breaker is being moved to SERVICE position. A crank or lever arrangement shall preferably be provided for smooth and positive movement of breaker between Service and Isolated positio

ns. 7. The rack out assembly shall have distinct SERVICE, TEST and ISOLATED positions. It should be possible t o close the breaker compartment door in isolated position also, so that the switchgear retains its specified degree of protection. All doors, removable covers and glass windows shall have neoprene gaskets all arou nd. 8. New enclosure parts are required which shall be fixed along with retrofitted breaker. It should be constr ucted with rolled steel sections. The doors and covers shall be constructed from cold rolled steel sheets of 2.0 mm or higher thickness. 9. The switchgear shall be cooled by natural air flow and forced cooling shall not be accepted. 10. Safety shutters shall be provided to cover up the fixed contacts on bus bar when the breaker is moved to ISOLATED position. The shutters should move automatically, through a linkage with the movement of th e breaker. A clearly visible warning label "Isolate elsewhere before opening" shall be provided on the shutt ers. Breaker compartment doors shall have pad locking facility. 11. The breaker and the auxiliary compartments provided on the front side shall have strong hinged doors. Breaker compartment doors shall have pad locking facility. 12. In the Service position, the breaker shall be so secured that it is not displaced by short circuit forces. Ju mpers and other components of the switchgear shall also be properly supported to withstand all possible s hort circuit forces corresponding to the short circuit rating specified. 13. The new enclosure shall be constructed with rolled steel sections. The doors shall be constructed from CRS sheets of 2 mm or higher thickness B. Circuit Breakers 1. The circuit breakers shall be of air break type. They shall comprise of three separate, identical single mo dular pole interrupting units, operated through a common shaft by a sturdy operating mechanism. Circuit Breakers should meet all the fault making and breaking capacities mentioned in ‘Technical Parameters’. A n arrangement of two breakers in parallel to meet a specified current rating shall not be acceptable. 2. Breaker shall have all internal release suitable for feeder protection. 3. Accessories like closing coil, shunt trip shall be of proper rating to avoid failures during breaker abnorm alities. 4. All the Accessories are to be pre-wired so as to ease installation with no critical setting. 5. The breaker shall be tested as per IS-13947-2 / IEC-60947-2. Manufacturer’s factory test certificates sho uld be supplied along with the breaker. Factory test certificate shall be valid from last 10 years from the d ate of incorporation of type test conducted from NABL accredited lab 6. It should be possible for the manufacturer to provide IP54 cover for the breaker. 7. Circuit breaker shall be of re-strike free, stored energy operated and trip free type. Motor wound closing spring charging shall only be acceptable. 8. There should be a mechanical indication for the breaker position - SERVICE, TEST and ISOLATED position s. It should also have a mechanical indication for SPRING CHARGED/DISCHARGED. 9. Interlocks shall be provided to ensure that the breaker shall close only in the Service, Test and Isolated positions when the breaker is in the cradle. But this should not prevent the breaker from closing in fully ret racted position (when it is on the trolley or a workbench). 10. Breaker should have manual mechanical trip and close mechanism also with lockable shroud. It should also be provided with manual spring charging mechanism. 11. The breakers shall have under voltage tripping and bypassing provision. 12. Breaker should have a non-resettable counter. 13. Breaker should have 6NO+6NC potential free auxiliary contacts for external use. 14. Spares like pole assembly & main operating mechanism should be available as standard spare & in cas e of failure of these it should be possible to replace them at the site. The vendor has to give a guarantee of

minimum 6 years for breaker spares availability 15. Isolating Contacts for main power circuit shall be silver plated, of self-aligning type, of robust design a nd capable of withstanding the specified short circuit currents. They shall preferably be shrouded with an i nsulating material. Plug and socket contacts for auxiliary circuits shall also be silver plated, sturdy and of s elf-aligning type having a high degree of reliability. 16. All working part of the mechanism shall be of corrosion resisting material. Bearings which require greas ing shall be equipped with pressure type grease fittings. Bearing pins, bolts, nuts and other parts shall be adequately secured and locked to prevent loosening or change in adjustment due to repeated operation of the breaker and the mechanism. 17. The operating mechanism shall be such that failure of any auxiliary spring shall not prevent tripping an d shall not lead to closing or tripping of circuit breaker. Failure of any auxiliary spring shall also not cause damage to the circuit breaker or endanger the operator. 18. Mechanical indicators shall be provided on the breaker to indicate OPEN / CLOSED conditions of the cir cuit breaker and CHARGED / DISCHARGED conditions of the closing spring. An operation counter shall also be provided. These shall be visible without opening the breaker compartment door. 19. The rated control supply voltage shall be as mentioned elsewhere under Technical parameters. The clo sing coil and spring charging motor shall operate satisfactorily at all values of control supply voltage betw een 85 and 110 percent of the rated voltage. 20. The shunt trip coil shall operate satisfactorily under all operating conditions of the circuit breaker up to its rated short circuit breaking current at all values of control supply voltage between 80 and 120 percent of the rated voltage. The trip coil shall be so designed that it does not get energized when its healthiness i s monitored by indicating lamps (Red) and one trip coil supervision relay. 21. The time taken for charging of closing spring shall not exceed 20 seconds. The spring charging shall take place automatically after a closing operation. Breaker operation shall be independent of the spring charging motor which shall only charge the closing spring. Opening spri ng shall get charged automatically during closing operation. 22. Spring charging motors shall be capable of starting and charging the closing spring twice in quick succ ession without exceeding acceptable winding temperature when the control supply voltage is anywhere be tween 85% and 110% of the rated voltage. The initial temperature shall be as prevalent in the switchgear panel during full load operation with 50 deg. C ambient air temperature. The motor shall be provided with s hort circuit protection. The manual spring charging lever should be available in breaker, so that the breake r’s spring can be charged, if aux supply of spring charging motor fails. 23. As long as power supply is available to the spring charging motor, a continuous sequence of closing an d opening operations shall be possible. One open-close- open operation of the circuit breaker shall be poss ible after failure of power supply to the motor of a closed breaker. 24. Motor windings shall be provided with class E insulation or better. The insulation shall be given tropical and fungicidal treatment for successful operation of the motor in a hot, humid and tropical climate. 25. Circuit breaker shall be provided with inter pole barriers of flame proof insulating materials. The use of inflammable materials shall not be acceptable. C. Control and Interlocks 1. The circuit breaker will normally be controlled from local by means of TNC switches mounted on a local control panel at approx. 15-meter distance from breaker. The location of local control panel will be provide d by NSPCL. It should also be possible to operate the breaker in TEST/SERVICE/SWITCHGEAR position by m eans of a TNC switch mounted on breaker control cubicle. Apart from that, provision should also be made i n breaker control cubicle for operating the breaker from remote. The remote control panels will be placed at the following locations: • CHP PCC • CW pump house PCC 2. The voltage level of ON/OFF commands will be freezed after award of contract and ON/OFF feedback will be C/N/O type unless otherwise specified.

3. The basic control scheme shall be developed as per the sample schematic logics and should be modifia ble for any changes at site. 4. Facilities shall be provided for mechanical tripping of the breaker and for manual charging of the stored energy mechanism for a complete duty cycle, in an emergency. 5. Each panel shall have two separate limit switches, one for the Service position and the other for TEST po sition. Each of these limit switches shall have at least TWO (2) contacts which shall close in the respective positions. 6. Movement of breaker between SERVICE and ISOLATED positions shall be mechanically prevented when t he breaker is closed. An attempt to withdraw a closed breaker shall not trip it rather the breaker draw-out mechanism shall become locked and inaccessible if breaker is ON. 7. Closing of the breaker shall be possible only when breaker is either in ISOLATED, TEST or in SERVICE pos ition and shall not be possible when breaker is in between. following conditions. i. OFF position feedback should be available in the following positions i.e. Breaker isolated or removed fro m compartment and OFF or Breaker in Service or Test position and OFF. ii. ON position feedback shall be available in the following positions i.e. Breaker in Service or Test position and ON. 9. Breaker disturbance signal shall be extended when Breaker NOT in Service position. 10. Breaker disturbance signal shall be extended when Breaker not ready to close if- Trip circuit not healthy. ii. Overload/Motor Start fail operated. iii. Electrical fault operated. iv. Spring not charged. v. Closing circuit control supply not available. vi. Emg. stop push button operated. 11. Suitable reliable arrangement should be provided to ensure that the remote feedback do not change in case of a Failure of control supply in the breaker panel when the breaker is in service. The additional NO & NC contacts of the breaker to be given through mechanical latch contactor/VAJC type relays or similar. 12. It shall be possible to easily make out whether the breaker in SERVICE OR ISOLATED POSITION even w hen the compartment door is closed. 4.0 AUXILIARY POWER SUPPLY: All the breakers that will be installed in outgoing feeders of switchboard shall be suitable for auxiliary pow er supply 110V AC with tolerance of 85% to 110% of rated voltage & shall be finalized during detailed engi neering. In each section of the switchgear there should be two nos of control transformers with main/stand by and auto switching of supply if one supply fails or vice versa. The vendor has to do the modification wor k of power supply and control supply in the existing switchgear. Vendor shall also install control bus in the existing switchgear panel for distribution of control supply. Breakers installed for incomers of switchboard shall be suitable for auxiliary power supply 220V DC with tol erance of 85% to 110% of rated voltage. The source of 220V DC will be supplied by NSPCL up to the switch board. Distribution of auxiliary power up to the breaker is in the scope of contractor II. SCOPE OF WORK FOR RETROFITTING The scope of work shall include design, manufacture, shop testing, supply, transportation & complete insur ance, handling and storage at site, complete installation, testing, retrofit and commissioning of 415V ACB t ype breakers with protection release in phased manner. 1.0 DETAILED SCOPE OF WORK (Vendor’s scope)

1. Unloading/loading of supplied panels components, breakers and other related material at site location s pecified by owner are in the scope of vendor. 2. Shifting of new breakers from the place of unloading to the proposed location of installation is in the sco pe of vendor. 3. Retrofitting of 415V breaker in the existing switchgears. 4. Protection setting calculation & implementation, building of logic diagrams for switchgear as per M/s NS PCL given scheme and requirement. All protection settings should be programmable and modifiable at site . The vendor has to set the protection as per the existing setting or detailed engineering to be done by the vendor for protection setting. 5. Dismantling of existing panel components wherever required. 6. Erection of all new components which are required. 7. Fitting of new panel door. 8. Pre commissioning test of all components. 9. Earthing of new system as per IS/IEC standards 10. Pre-commissioning tests of Retrofitted breaker. 11. Pre-commissioning test of protection releases. 12. Shifting of dismantled panels from switchgear to the place specified by the owner at site. 13. Complete internal, inter-panel & intra-panel cabling/ wiring which include laying, designing & terminati on required for complete commissioning of the system. 14. Preparation & submission of test reports, commissioning records after completion of work. 15. The entire requirement shall be evaluated and finalized by the bidder during detailed engineering in co nsultation with the owner. 16. In CHP MCC/ Dredge pump house MCC/CW pump house PCC/HP-LP pump house MCC, a separate contro l supply of 110V AC to be provided by the vendor with necessary wires/cables. 17. Indication lamps should be LED with LVGP features to avoid mal-operation of breakers due to LED failu re. 2.0 EXCLUSIONS FROM SCOPE OF WORK 1. All building and major civil works. 2. Auxiliary 220V DC Power supply at terminal point for operation of breaker shall be in owner's scope. 3.0 INPUT FROM THE VENDOR 1. The vendor shall be responsible for collecting all the information or data of existing equipment/ material / systems. The Owner shall only assist the contractor wherever possible to provide information /data. 2. The vendor shall identify all interface issues with owner, and shall be responsible for such interfacing, c oordination and exchange of all necessary information. 3. The vendor shall make his own necessary arrangements for boarding and lodging arrangement for their personnel. 4. All testing instruments, tools and tackles required for erection, testing and commissioning of breaker an d the Protection system are in the scope of vendor. He shall also produce a valid certificate of calibration f or all measuring instruments used. 4.0 DRAWING AND DOCUMENTS 1. Minimum six sets of final as built drawing, six sets of O&M manual, engineering data, factory test report s, site test & commissioning reports shall be submitted by the vendor in hard copy. 2. Vendor shall also submit as built drawings and manuals in hard copies as well as soft copies

5.0 DEVIATIONS 1. The Bidder is required to submit with his proposal a detailed list of any and all exceptions taken to this s pecification. 2. In absence of such a list, it will be understood and agreed that Bidder’s proposal is based on strict confo rmance to this specification in all respects. 3. The requirement is not intended to prohibit Bidders from offering alternative quotations for equipment w hich they consider equal to or superior to that specified for the intended service and for which he believes he can show economic and/or technical advantages. 6.0 SUPPLY OF EQUIPMENT AND MATERIAL 1. The vendor shall be responsible for design, engineering, manufacture, testing & inspection at manufact urer works, supply transportation, insurance, delivery at site, complete erection and supervision, site testin g and inspection and successful commissioning of all the equipment and materials listed at Bill of Quantitie s of the specification, detailed elsewhere in specification and as shown in the tender drawing. 2. Any item though not specifically mentioned but is required to complete the retrofitting works in all respe ct for its safe, reliable, and efficient and trouble-free operation shall also be taken to be included and same shall be supplied and erected by the party without any extra cost. 3. The quantities of equipment/ material indicated in PR, indicated in this specification are for the purpose of bidding only. Any item which is not mentioned in PR but essential as per technical specification, then ve ndor shall quote for them also. 4. The vendor shall, however supply and erect and construct as per the quantities finalized during / after d etailed engineering, execution of works and shall be paid accordingly. 5. All consumables, wastages and damages shall be to the account of the vendor. 7.0 ERECTION WORKS 1. The vendor shall construct, erect and install all the equipment and material for retrofitting of 415V Switc hgear’s LT breakers covered under the PR. 2. The vendor shall be responsible for provision of all labour, tools, plants and supervisory staff for safe, re liable, proper and correct erection of project components. 3. The vendor shall ensure periodic cleaning of work sites and removal of all waste material, packing mate rial and leftovers and their proper disposal. 4. As the work is to be carried out in an existing charged power plant, the party has to employ competent manpower and supervision personnel. 5. The vendor is solely and fully responsible for the safety of personnel and materials. Any damages to the existing equipment shall be made good by the party as directed by the Engineer–In- Charge at no extra co st to the Owner. 8.0 FUNCTIONAL GUARANTEE AND LIQUIDATED DAMAGE 1. The bidder shall guarantee that equipment offered shall meet the rating and performance requirement s tipulated for various equipment covered in the specification. The bidder shall also furnish a declaration in t he schedule provided for the purpose in bid forms. 2. If the guarantees are not established at factory tests, then the owner at his discretion may reject the eq uipment or accept it after assessing. 3. Vendor has to ensure that no tripping takes place due to mal-operation of release or due to improper co nfiguration/settings. For every tripping attributable to above reason, a justification needs to be submitted by the party. In case the problems persist M/s NSPCL may request supplier to change the release. Still if th e problem persists M/s NSPCL may impose a penalty. The value of penalty shall be limited to a maximum 5 % value of Commissioning portion only. The detail of Liquidated damages to be paid for delay shall be as under:

A-DELIVERY: a. The circuit breakers and materials will be deemed to have been delivered only when all its components and parts are also delivered. If certain materials are not delivered in time, the equipment shall be consider ed as undelivered till missing parts are delivered. b. The Liquidated damages for delay in supply shall be one half of one percent (1/2%) of the total contract value, per week. B- RETROFITTING: a. The retrofitting of the breakers shall be deemed completed only when successful load trial for 1 month i s completed. b. The Liquidated damages for delay in successful trial operation on account of the contractor within the es tipulate time under the contract shall be one half of one percent (1/2%) of the total value of ACB & retrofitt ing charges (pro rata basis) per week. Liquidated Damage for material delivery & Retrofitting shall be evaluated separately & there shall be ceilin g of five percent (5%) of total contract value as a whole. 9.0 DEFECT LIABILITY 1. The defect liability period shall be 12 months from the date of successful commissioning of the breakers on pro rata basis. 2.
